resources.string: That time hasn’t come yet. Pick an earlier time.
Change your search or clear the filters.
A chart of your max weight and estimated 1RM will appear after your first workouts.
PRs will appear after your first workout with this exercise.
“%1$s” will be removed from your exercise list.
Select at least one primary muscle
This exercise is in a routine, your history or an ongoing workout, so it can’t be deleted.
Create your own or start from a ready-made template.
“%1$s” will be removed from the list. Completed workouts stay in your history.
Finish or discard your current workout before starting another one.
Unsaved changes to this routine will be lost.
Leave blank for no target weight
Three days: push, pull and legs. The classic split for 3 or 6 workouts a week.
Two days: upper and lower body. Good for 4 workouts a week.
Full body every workout, alternating A and B. A good start with 3 workouts a week.
Deleting the last set removes the exercise from this workout.
Add your first exercise to get started.
The workout will be added to your history.
No sets are checked off, so the workout won’t be saved.
Couldn’t save the workout. Try again.
All sets from this workout will be lost.
In this workout, your targets differed from the routine. Choose what to save to the routine.
Workout time, set progress and rest countdown. No sound; a vibration signals the end of rest.

During a workout, GymTracker shows the time, set progress and rest countdown in a notification, on the lock screen and in the Now Bar. The notification is silent; a vibration signals the end of rest. Without permission, workouts still work, but you won’t see any of this.
The end-of-rest alert and the notification on the lock screen or in the Now Bar may not come through.
Everything that determines whether a workout shows up as a live notification (Now Bar) and whether rest works with the screen off. After changing settings, come back here and the list will refresh.

The Now Bar only shows apps allowed in Settings → Lock screen and AOD → Now Bar. On some One UI versions, you also need to turn on “Live notifications for all apps” in Developer options. To enable Developer options, tap “Build number” 7 times (About phone → Software information); while they’re off, the button below opens that screen.
Your finished workouts will appear here, along with PRs and charts.
Exercises will appear here after your first finished workout.
Routines will appear here after your first workout from a routine.
Warm-ups excluded. A set counts toward the muscle groups of the exercise’s primary muscles.
The workout will be removed from your history, and PRs and charts will be recalculated without it.
Couldn’t delete the workout. Try again.
Fill in reps for every set or delete the empty set.
Unsaved changes to the workout will be lost.
GymTracker runs entirely on this phone: no account, server, ads or analytics. It reads Health Connect data only with your permission, separately for each feature.

Exercise sessions, heart rate and calories; weight, height and body composition; steps and distance; sleep, resting heart rate and HRV. With additional permissions, also data older than 30 days and background reading.
To show heart rate, zones and calories for workouts linked to a watch session, watch sessions in your history, steps and body measurements, and an approximate readiness to train.
Nothing, until you turn on saving workouts. Then each finished workout goes to Health Connect as a strength training session: name, start and end.
Data that’s read goes into a separate database on this phone, which Android backup skips. The app never sends or shares it. It uses the internet only to fetch exercise photos.
You can revoke permissions at any time in Health Connect. “Disconnect” on the app’s Health Connect screen revokes all permissions and deletes the imported data; your workouts stay.
Heart rate and sessions from your watch, body measurements, steps and sleep from other apps. Everything stays on this phone.
Health Connect isn’t available on this phone. The app works the same without it, just without watch data.
Without permission, this feature is off. If the permission window didn’t appear, you can turn it on in Health Connect.
Exercise sessions, heart rate and calories. For a workout linked to a watch session, you’ll see heart rate, zones and calories, and other sessions go to your history.
Weight, height and body composition, e.g. from a smart scale.
Steps, distance and calories for the whole day.
Sleep, resting heart rate and HRV for a rough estimate of training readiness.
Without this permission, Health Connect only shares data from 30 days before the first connection. With it, we’ll also import older sessions, measurements and sleep.
Health Connect is temporarily limiting requests. The rest of the data will come in with the next sync.
Every hour when the battery isn’t low. Requires a separate permission.
Every workout you finish from now on goes to Health Connect as strength training. We don’t save workouts linked to a watch session.
If your watch also records the workout, it will show up in Health Connect twice: from the watch and from GymTracker. We don’t save workouts linked to a watch session.
We calculate them from your max heart rate. If you don’t enter one, we estimate them from your age: 208 − 0.7 × age.
We’ll revoke all permissions and delete the imported data. Your workouts stay, and links to watch sessions come back when you reconnect.
Disconnected. Android will revoke the permissions when you close the app, and you can reconnect once you open it again.
Heart rate and watch sessions, body measurements, steps and sleep
Enter your age or max heart rate on the Health Connect screen to see time in zones.
No heart rate data from this session.
This session is no longer in Health Connect.
Session from Health Connect. You can change it in the app that saved it.
No sessions from 12 hours before or after this workout.
A rough estimate compared with your 7-day average. This isn’t a medical assessment.
Collecting data. A score will appear after a few days of sleep, resting heart rate or HRV.
Connect recovery in Health Connect: sleep, resting heart rate and HRV give a rough readiness estimate.
You don’t have any routines yet. Start an empty workout or build a routine, and I’ll suggest the next one.
Work out this week to start a streak.
A workout this week will extend your streak.
Your last workout will show up here with its duration, sets and volume.
No PRs in the last 7 days. Every workout is a new chance.
Connect Health Connect and steps from your phone and watch will show up here.
Add your weight and height in Profile, and I’ll show your trend and BMI here.
Add your height to calculate BMI.
Drag to reorder. The switch shows or hides a widget.
A rough guide: BMI doesn’t tell muscle from fat.
Masses are calculated from your latest weight and body fat. Enter skeletal muscle manually, since Health Connect doesn’t store it.
Without body fat, lean mass comes from Health Connect and fat mass is the rest of the weight from the same weigh-in. Enter skeletal muscle manually, since Health Connect doesn’t store it.
BMI will appear once you add weight and height.
No measurements. Add your first one or connect Health Connect to get them from a scale or watch.
%1$s from %2$s will be removed from your profile and charts.
Connect Health Connect to see active and total calories from your phone and watch.
No calorie data from the last 7 days.
This palette has a fixed brightness, so Light and Dark mode don’t change it.
Pure black in the dark theme.
Not available with a black-and-white palette.
Matte backgrounds instead of glass, and stronger contrast.
Always stored in kg; pounds only change what you see and enter. Progression adds 2.5 kg or 5 lb.
Used when an exercise in a routine has none of its own.
Notification sound; silent mode and Do Not Disturb mute it.

A backup is one file with your routines, workouts, measurements and custom exercises. It doesn’t include settings or Health Connect data; those come back with sync. Import also accepts a backup from GymTracker v1.
Couldn’t save the backup. Try again or choose a different location.
Finish or discard the workout in progress to import a backup.
Once a day, when you open the app
This test build doesn’t check for updates. Install a newer one from the APK file on GitHub Releases.
You have the latest version. Checked %1$s, %2$s.
Couldn’t check. Check your internet connection.
Android installs updates only from apps you allow. Turn on “Allow from this source” for GymTracker and come back, and the installation will start on its own.
Checking the file’s signature and handing it to the system installer. After installation the app will close; open it again.
Couldn’t download the file. Check your internet connection and try again.
This release has no APK file.
The downloaded file isn’t signed with the same key as the installed app, so it wasn’t installed.
The system didn’t install the update. Try again.
Libraries, fonts, icons and the exercise database the app uses.
This isn’t a GymTracker backup. Your data hasn’t changed.
The file is damaged or incomplete. Your data hasn’t changed.
This backup is from a newer version of the app. Update GymTracker and try again.
This GymTracker v1 backup is from an older version. Update v1, make a new backup and import it.
Replace your data with the backup?
Replace your data with the v1 backup?
Your current data will be replaced and the app will restart. Your previous data will stay on the phone as a backup.
